[&larr; Back to Datasets](../index.qmd)

The "final form" of this dataset evolved over a few stages:

* First, Jeff announced in class that the dataset would comprise [UN Comtrade](https://comtradeplus.un.org/) data merged with vessel arrival and departure data from [IMF PortWatch](https://portwatch.imf.org/pages/data-and-methodology). Unfortunately, Georgetown does not subscribe to Comtrade, so I'm unable to bulk-export that data
* Next, we tried the UN Food and Agriculture Organization's FAOSTAT ["Detailed Trade Matrix"](https://www.fao.org/faostat/en/#data/TM): this dataset *is* available in full, but is **aggregated** to the (sender, receiver, product, year) level
* For the **microdata** we really want – so that we can simulate the kind of **individual financial transaction data** that you might encounter as a data scientist in **Retail Sales**, it turns out that Colombia's *Departamento Administrativo Nacional de Estadística (DANE)* provides individual-transaction level data!

With that note on the trajectory of this dataset out of the way, here is your vignette and accompanying sample midterm questions:

## Data Access

Here, for ease of use, we have **translated** the (abbreviated) column headers into simpler-to-understand English versions. The codebook is as follows:

| Column Name | Translation | Description |
| - | - | - |
| `FECH` | `date` | `FECH` is short for *fecha*, meaning **"date"**. Here, the date has **four digits**, where the first two represent the year and the second two represent the month: `YYMM`. |
| `ADUA` | `customs_house` | `ADUA` is short for *aduana*, meaning "customs house". Here, the specific sub-department of the customs declaration is encoded as an **integer**. Department `3`, for example, processed over 10K exports in January 2025, whereas department `27` processed only 1. (Note that all of the department codes may not used within a given year, meaning that you shouldn't assume that you can loop from `1` to `n`) |
| `PAIS` | `country` | `PAIS` is the ASCII version of *país*, meaning "country". It is a **numeric** variable, a three-digit code representing the country that the good(s) were imported from / exported to. For example, imports from / exports to the United States have code `840`. |
| `COD_PAI4` | `country_code` | For each value of `PAIS`, this value is the corresponding `string`-valued **three-letter code** for the country. For example, imports from / exports to the United States have `COD_PAI4` value `USA`. |
| `COD_SAL1` | `departure_point_code1` | `COD_SAL` and `COD_SAL1` are both short for *código lugar de salida*, meaning "departure point". `COD_SAL1` is a *numeric* (integer) code for the point of departure. For example, the port of [Cartagena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cartagena,_Colombia) is represented by `6`. |
| `COD_SAL` | `departure_point_code` | `COD_SAL` and `COD_SAL1` are both short for *código lugar de salida*, meaning "departure point". `COD_SAL` is a `string`-valued **three-letter code** for the point of departure. For example, the port of [Cartagena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cartagena,_Colombia) is represented as `"CTG"`. |
| `DPTO2` | `department` | *departamento* |
| `VIA` | `via` | |
| `BANDERA` | `flag` | |
